newsitem.title: INDIA: Templeton, Threadneedle raise targeted India funds.
newsitem.headline: Templeton, Threadneedle raise targeted India funds.

text.p: Templeton India Asset Management Company and ITC Threadneedle Asset Management Company said on Monday their maiden domestic mutual funds had each raised the targeted 500 million rupees from public subcriptions.

"We have crossed 52 crores (520 million rupees) according to rough figures," B. Swaminathan, Templeton's vice president (operations) said. "Lots of (outstation) centres have not yet reported (their collections)," he said.
Templeton had sought an extension of its earlier closing date of August 26 to August 31 following lukewarm response to its offer. It had said it will not retain oversubscription.
ITC Threadneedle extended its closing date by three days to September 4. "We have already crossed the target," Sanjay Jha, vice president (marketing) said.
Unlike Templeton, ITC Threadneedle does not have a cap and intends to retain oversubscription, he said.
Both funds had opened for subscription on August 19.

Jha admitted to poor response from retail investors. "People are still bearish (about the market)," he said. "And mutual funds have not developed the kind of attraction that comes only from a track record," he said.
He said ITC Threadneedle would deploy funds on identified stocks within two weeks of collecting the subscriptions.

ITC Threadneedle is equally owned by Threadneedle of U.K. and India's ITC Classic Finance. Templeton India is 75 percent owned by Franklin Templeton Group of U.S. and 25 percent by Indian industrialist Rajan Raheja.
